notes:
Summary: Archipelago runs a legacy media archive service (news reels, 40+ years of transcripts, production notes). Primary problem: search quality for long noisy transcripts + fast discovery for editors. They want RAG-style retrieval with embeddings + a trained reranker to handle long-document signal (lead paragraphs, timestamps, speaker turns).

Key constraints:
- Corpus: ~20M documents (mix of multi-hour transcripts and short metadata items). Typical long doc 30k-80k tokens; many tiny metadata rows.
- Latency SLO: interactive editing workflow <= 250ms for initial results, 100-300ms acceptable for reranker stage (editor tolerance). CTO quote: "If it feels slow, editors won't adopt it — target under 200ms 90th perc."
- Cost sensitivity: want < $0.02/query (average) including embedding lookup + reranker. Will accept higher cost for premium editorial tier.

Technical discussion notes (shorthand):
- Indexing scale: plan to precompute embeddings for all chunks; expect index size 1.2-1.8 TB depending on model. Discussed compact embeddings (quantized e5 variants) to reduce index footprint.
- Chunking: two approaches on table: 1) small-chunk strategy (1k token chunks, 20% overlap) — pros: fine-grain retrieval, cons: explosion of vectors and higher recall cost; 2) coarse-chunk strategy (3k-4k tokens w/ speaker-boundary-aware splits, 10% overlap) — pros: fewer vectors, preserves context for reranker, cons: embedding quality drop if chunk too long. Team leaning toward hybrid: pre-split by scene/segment; default chunk 1k tokens for transcripts, 3k for long-form docs with metadata dense.
- Retriever topology: HNSW for approximate nearest neighbor; plan periodic reindex to incorporate updated metadata. Considering tiered routing: cheap ANN for broad recall, then cross-encoder reranker on top-K.
- Reranker design: cross-encoder fine-tuned on domain pairs (query, chunk) using human relevance labels. SE note: cross-encoder gives 2-8x quality boost but requires GPU for low-latency; exploring distilled bi-encoder -> cross-encoder cascade to reduce GPU calls.
- Cost model: initial estimates: embedding lookup + ANN ~ $0.003-0.007 per query; cross-encoder rerank for top-50 using a small quantized model ~ $0.01-0.03/query depending on batching and GPU utilization. Need POC to narrow numbers.

POC scope agreed:
- 2-week proof: 200k sample of corpus (mix of long transcripts + metadata), implement hybrid chunking, build FAISS/HNSW index, run query set (1k editorial queries), measure recall@10/50, reranker latency P90, and cost per query.
- Deliverables: cost-per-query spreadsheet, recommended chunking policy, reranker model spec and throughput plan, fallback routing policy to cheaper models under load.

Stated preferences: prefer open models for embeddings (e5-family, open-embedding-large) and an option to use Redwood-verified quantized rerankers. Legal wants explicit data-residency in EU for archival footage from EU broadcasters.
